paper_metadata.title: Quantum vs. Classical Machine Learning: A Benchmark Study for Financial Prediction

experiments.description: Directional return classification on Turkish equities using low-dimensional technical indicators, comparing QNN variants against an ANN baseline on a 3-feature setup.

algorithm.variant: QNN family (SQ, MQ, Hybrid-SQ, Hybrid-MQ) for directional classification
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized rotation gates (Rx, Ry, Rz) with entangling operations
algorithm.convergence_criteria: selected by highest mean validation AUC across 5 expanding-window folds

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3-dimensional feature vector from Turkish equities is mapped to 3 qubits; each feature requires a dedicated qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary next-day direction prediction y_t = 1 if P_t > P_{t-1}, else 0

problem_instance.description: Directional classification for Turkish equities using momentum indicators.

dataset_specification.description: Tickers: KCHOL.IS, GARAN.IS, TUPRS.IS, ULKER.IS, TCELL.IS. Adjusted close prices used. Features: RSI-14, %K-14, 3-day moving average of %K-14. Walk-forward expanding-window cross-validation with 5 folds; final fold test period 2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31, training period 2009-01-07 to 2019-12-31.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Adjusted-close prices converted to momentum indicators; min-max scaling to [0,1] fitted on training fold only; expanding-window CV.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean AUC across 5 validation folds; final fold reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max normalization; optional classical preprocessing layer for Hybrid variants mapping R^d to R^q.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Single-qubit readout rescaled from [-1,1] to [0,1] or multi-qubit readout aggregated through a classical dense layer.

speedup_claims.conditions: Directional classification on Turkish equities with 3-D technical indicators
speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup or runtime comparison is reported; only predictive metrics are compared.

experiments.description: Directional return classification on the S&P 500 using medium-dimensional cross-asset features, comparing QNN variants against an ANN baseline on a 7-feature setup.

algorithm.variant: QNN family (SQ, MQ, Hybrid-SQ, Hybrid-MQ) for directional classification
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized rotation gates (Rx, Ry, Rz) with entangling operations
algorithm.convergence_criteria: selected by highest mean validation AUC across 5 expanding-window folds

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 7-dimensional feature vector is mapped to 7 qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary next-day direction prediction y_t = 1 if P_t > P_{t-1}, else 0

problem_instance.description: Directional classification for S&P 500 using cross-asset lagged returns.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance S&P 500 and global index universe

dataset_specification.description: Target: S&P 500 close price. Features: same-day log-returns of Nikkei 225, Hang Seng, All Ordinaries, DAX, FTSE 100, plus lagged Dow Jones and NYSE Composite. Close-to-close protocol with U.S. proxies lagged by one day. Walk-forward expanding-window cross-validation with 5 folds; final fold test period 2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Min-max scaling to [0,1] fitted on training fold only; expanding-window CV; cross-asset lag alignment to avoid look-ahead bias.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean AUC across 5 validation folds; final fold reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max normalization; optional classical preprocessing layer for Hybrid variants mapping R^d to R^q.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Single-qubit readout rescaled from [-1,1] to [0,1] or multi-qubit readout aggregated through a classical dense layer.

speedup_claims.conditions: Directional classification on S&P 500 with 7 cross-asset features
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime or asymptotic speedup is reported.

experiments.description: Directional return classification on U.S. equities using high-dimensional cross-asset and self-return features, comparing QNN variants against ANN baselines on a 64-feature setup.

algorithm.variant: QNN family (SQ, MQ, Hybrid-SQ, Hybrid-MQ) for directional classification
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized rotation gates (Rx, Ry, Rz) with entangling operations
algorithm.convergence_criteria: selected by highest mean validation AUC across 5 expanding-window folds

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 64-dimensional feature vector is embedded using amplitude encoding; the paper states this reduces the requirement to n = 6 qubits for 64 features, with n treated as a hyperparameter in {2,...,6}.
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary next-day direction prediction y_t = 1 if P_t > P_{t-1}, else 0

problem_instance.description: Directional classification for selected U.S. equities using self-lagged returns and global cross-asset returns.

dataset_specification.description: Tickers: AAPL, BA, GILD, DVN, LNC. Features: 8 days of self returns plus 7-day returns of eight global indices (56 features) for a total of 64 features. Walk-forward expanding-window cross-validation with 5 folds; final fold test period 2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Min-max scaling to [0,1] fitted on training fold only; lag-matrix embedding; expanding-window CV.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean AUC across 5 validation folds; final fold reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max normalization; optional classical preprocessing layer for Hybrid variants mapping R^d to R^q.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Single-qubit readout rescaled from [-1,1] to [0,1] or multi-qubit readout aggregated through a classical dense layer.

speedup_claims.conditions: Directional classification on U.S. equities with 64-dimensional amplitude-encoded features
speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is reported; the paper only discusses predictive performance and qubit-count feasibility.

experiments.description: Live-trading simulation on the S&P 500 comparing QLSTM and classical LSTM across four market regimes, with threshold-based trading and Sharpe-optimized calibration.

algorithm.ansatz: variational quantum circuits replacing LSTM gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: early stopping when ES AUC fails to improve for 30 epochs; model selected by highest AUC on meta slice; thresholds selected by maximum Sharpe on calibration slice

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input features are mapped through a classical linear embedding into qubit rotations; each VQC block uses a hybrid input layer and multi-qubit Z-basis readout.
problem_formulation.objective_function: predict next-day return direction and convert probabilities into long/short/neutral trading signals to maximize risk-adjusted return
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold-based trading rule with no-trade region; transaction costs applied when position changes.

problem_instance.description: S&P 500 live-trading/backtesting across four historical regimes.

dataset_specification.description: S&P 500 index from 2008-2024, segmented into four regimes: F1 2008-01-02 to 2009-12-31, F2 2018-01-02 to 2019-12-31, F3 2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31, F4 2022-01-03 to 2024-12-31. Features: previous-day log return, MACD line, MACD signal, RSI-14. Rolling windows of length 10. Expanding-window cross-validation with 4 folds and 70/10/10/10 split per fold.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Adjusted-close prices; min-max scaling to [0,1] fitted on training portion only; threshold calibration on hold-out slice; backtest includes transaction costs.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: AUC, annualized return, annualized standard deviation, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio; final thresholds chosen to maximize Sharpe on calibration slice.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Min-max scaling; classical linear embedding before quantum gates; weighted BCE loss during training.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Probability outputs converted to trading signals using thresholds tau_long and tau_short; backtesting with transaction costs.

speedup_claims.conditions: Live trading on S&P 500 across four market regimes
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime or computational speedup is reported; only trading-performance comparisons are provided.

experiments.description: Realized volatility forecasting using QSVR with angle encoding, compared against classical SVR kernels and GARCH on four equities.

algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient RY-RZ rotations with ring of CZ entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: best hyperparameters selected by Optuna on expanding-window training; retrain on full in-sample window and predict one-step ahead

hyperparameters.feature_map: U_rot RY(x)^{⊗ d} repeated L times

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical feature vector of lagged returns and realized variance is embedded into a quantum feature map; kernel computed from exact statevector overlaps.
problem_formulation.objective_function: one-step-ahead realized variance prediction y_{t+1} = RV_{t+1}

problem_instance.description: One-step-ahead realized volatility forecasting for S&P 500, AAPL, GARAN, and KCHOL using lagged returns and realized variance.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance equities with realized variance features

dataset_specification.description: Assets: S&P 500, AAPL, GARAN.IS, KCHOL.IS. Target is 5-day rolling realized variance RV_t = (1/5) sum_{i=0}^4 r_{t-i}^2. Features are past p returns and past q realized variances. Expanding-window forecasting with initial training set of 720 days; retraining every 120 days; total training window lengths L in {1000, 2000, 3000, 4000} days.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Standard scaling (z-score) implied by figure caption for volatility study; precomputed kernel matrix from simulated statevectors; one-step-ahead forecasting.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: QLIKE, MSE, R2, directional accuracy, and Diebold-Mariano tests against classical baselines.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Past returns and past realized variance; expanding-window retraining; Optuna hyperparameter search.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Precomputed kernel matrix fed to SVR; final one-step-ahead realized variance prediction.

speedup_claims.conditions: Realized volatility forecasting with quantum kernels on four equities
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports kernel-evaluation complexity O(N^2) but does not demonstrate a speedup over classical methods.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Kernel evaluation scales as O(N^2) where N is the number of samples
